qs.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with progressive memory loss and personality changes. MRI shows medial temporal lobe atrophy and posterior cortical atrophy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Frontotemporal dementia with asymmetric frontal atrophy
Alzheimer's disease with hippocampal volume loss
Vascular dementia with multiple lacunar infarctions
Normal pressure hydrocephalus with ventricular dilation
qs.e: Medial temporal lobe atrophy combined with posterior cortical atrophy is the classic radiological presentation of Alzheimer's disease.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: Radiology Exam - November 20, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A brain CT scan demonstrates marked prominence of the ventricles and sulci, consistent with medial temporal lobe atrophy, posterior atrophy, and frontal cortical atrophy. Which of the following represents this overall finding?
qs.e: Prominent sulci and ventricles reflect generalized cerebral atrophy rather than normal aging or isolated edema.
